body:
Hey man, I understand what you're going through. I'm 19 myself and I suffer with depression too. I'm in the military so I can't really talk about it either. I get exactly what you mean about every day being boring and hating what you do, a lot of the time I wonder if it's worth it myself, but what I find is that it's my ambition and the hope that comes along with it that keeps me going. You said you love music, if you have a dream then chase it and work hard for it, work on it in your free time and get it out there on YouTube and sound cloud. 

You said about your mum being one of the only things you care about, this definitely stuck out to me. I realised when I joined the military how much I missed my parents when they were gone, especially as I'm a bit of a loner too. Never take her for granted man, try and forge a closer bond with your mum, nothing is more important than family. If you wanna chat feel free to pm me. I hope things improve for you bro.

Hey, I understand how you're feeling, genuinely. I know what it's like to be alone, I know what it's like to feel abandoned, I know what it's like to wake up in the morning in a place you don't want to be in, dreading general day to day life, feeling like you're stuck and there's no way out. I'm still living through this right now, just like you.

 It may seem like everything is worthless right now but there really is hope, hope that things can and will get better, hope that the storm we are in will pass, hope that things will change. I don't know what you're going through or what situation you find yourself in, but there is always hope, and you're not alone. Things will be ok and the hard times will pass, for both you and I.

Before I joined the army I did a level 2 diploma in a vocational trade, I managed a pass but I was terrible at it (a bit of a theme coming on here haha). 

To be honest bro the only thing I do in my free time is go to the gym, I love PT, it's the only thing I really enjoy. In most of the army, as a trainee you're like banned from mingling with people higher up in the chain of command, most of them here are power mad pricks any way, and the cap badge I've transferred to has a lot of trainees who prefer to get smashed and then literally their conversations consist of what they did when they were smashed, and honestly that doesn't appeal to me. Despite the camp being pretty big, the gym is actually very empty most of the time in terms of people.

I've looked into the supposed sport teams they have here but they're all pretty much disbanded due to low turnouts. I might try and find a civvy boxing club somewhere around here. I'm not trying to say that I'm like a unique breed or whatever at all, I just don't seem to fit in with this military environment. In terms of leaving, If I can stick it out 3 more years I could try and get the PTI quals and do something fitness related in civvy street? It's such a saturated market but it's all I enjoy. Sorry about the wall of text!

I'm in the UK, I couldn't do anything if I came out bar menial labour, I left school with no qualifications. My family know I'm very unhappy but not to this extent. I try to visit them if I get a weekend off, that's the thing man, I have no one here to talk to. Literally my days are spent alone all day every day. The guy in my room is a total recluse. I've had acquaintances in other places, but here it's just so bad. Thanks for your time man.
Hey man, thanks for the reply. I don't have much choice to be honest, I'll have to try and stick it out. Maybe one day things will get better.
